title: Understanding Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a society's structured hierarchy, creating layers that assign unequal access to resources, power, and prestige. This institutional structure means that certain groups systematically possess more advantages than others, regardless of individual merit or talent.

Theoretical approaches provide varying explanations for this inequality. Functionalism often argues that differences in status are functional because they incentivize individuals to fill necessary societal roles. Conversely, conflict theory posits that stratification is a mechanism through which dominant groups maintain their power and privilege at the expense of subordinate classes.
